Our observations reveal ten new sources at a redshift of ∼ 6.9 (and three additional foreground galaxies at z ∼ 1-3) in the field around the two main, previously identified massive galaxies of the system

findings_qualitative.value: The core of the SPT0311-58 protocluster (r < 0.2 R_200) is likely not yet in virial equilibrium, though most member galaxies appear gravitationally bound to the dark-matter halo.

evidence.quote: A basic analysis indicates that the innermost regions of the protocluster (r < 0.2 R 200 ) have likely not yet reached virial equilibrium. We also located the galaxies in the projected phase space (PPS) diagram, and find that most are gravitationally bound to the halo.

findings_qualitative.value: The galaxies in SPT0311-58 exhibit diverse ISM ionisation and metallicity conditions, ranging from low-metallicity high-excitation conditions typical of z > 6 field galaxies in the external sources to nearly solar metallicity and lower log([O III]/H-beta) near the massive E and W galaxies.

evidence.quote: Their ionisation conditions range from those typical of the field galaxies at similar redshift recently studied with JWST to those found in more evolved objects at lower redshift, with log([OIII]/Hβ) varying from ∼ 0.25 to 1. The metallicity spans more than 0.8 dex across the FoV, reaching nearly solar values in some cases.

findings_qualitative.value: The E galaxy exhibits a metallicity gradient of ~0.1 dex/kpc (0.7 dex peak-to-peak), an unsettled turbulent ionised gas disc (v/sigma_0 ~ 1), velocity offsets and higher velocity dispersions in [O III] compared to ALMA [C II] in the south/east, and a likely pre-collision minor merger with L7.

evidence.quote: The detailed spatially resolved spectroscopy of the E galaxy reveals that it is actively assembling its stellar mass, showing inhomogeneities in the ISM properties at subkiloparsec scales, and a metallicity gradient (∼ 0.1 dex/kpc) that can be explained by accretion of low metallicity gas from the intergalactic medium.
The kinematic maps also depict an unsettled disc characterised by deviations from regular rotation, elevated turbulence, and indications of a possible precollision minor merger.

claims.hypothesis: SPT0311-58 resides at the core of an extremely massive protocluster at z ~ 6.9.
claims.experiment: Searched for and spectroscopically confirmed companion galaxies in the 17 x 17 kpc^2 JWST/NIRSpec IFU FoV, measured their radial velocities, stellar and dynamical masses, and estimated the dark-matter halo mass and dynamical state.
claims.result: Confirmed 10 new galaxies at z ~ 6.9 with dynamical masses of ~10^9 to 10^10 M_sun and radial velocity spread ~1500 km s^-1, yielding a number density phi ~ 10^4 Mpc^-3 and halo mass M_h ~ (5 +/- 3) x 10^12 M_sun; K-S test gives p = 0.04 for velocity normality.
claims.finding: SPT0311-58 is confirmed to be at the core of the most massive protocluster discovered so far at the Epoch of Reionisation, with a core that is likely not yet fully virialised.

evidence.quote: The implied large number density (ϕ ∼ 10 4 Mpc −3 ) and the wide spread in velocities confirm that SPT0311–58 is at the core of a protocluster immersed in a very massive dark-matter halo of ∼ (5 ± 3) × 10 12 M ⊙ , and therefore represents the most massive protocluster ever found at the epoch of reionisation (EoR).
We also studied the dynamical stage of its core and find that it is likely not fully virialised.

claims.hypothesis: Galaxies within the dense SPT0311-58 protocluster environment span a wide range of evolutionary stages, ISM conditions, and star formation obscuration regimes.
claims.experiment: Measured optical emission line ratios (N2-BPT, O32-R23), gas-phase metallicities, Balmer/Paschen dust attenuations, and H-alpha star formation rates across all z ~ 6.9 sources and compared with ALMA FIR/submm measurements.
claims.result: log([O III]/H-beta) ranges from ~0.25 to 1 and 12+log(O/H) spans ~0.8 dex (from 7.79 in L5 to 8.56 in C3). Dust-corrected SFR(H-alpha) recovers ~70-80% of total SFR in E (231-377 M_sun yr^-1), ~20% in heavily obscured W (603 M_sun yr^-1, A_V = 5.8 mag), and newly discovered galaxies contribute only a few percent.
claims.finding: The protocluster hosts galaxies across diverse evolutionary stages and three distinct star-formation/obscuration regimes, from metal-poor unobscured companions to evolved, metal-rich, heavily obscured central starbursts.

evidence.quote: The galaxies in the system exhibit a wide range of properties and evolutionary stages. The contribution of the ongoing Hα-based unobscured SFR to the total star formation (SF) varies significantly across the galaxies in the system.
Using Hα, we characterised the unobscured star formation (SFR(Hα)) in the system, and identified three distinct SF regimes.

claims.hypothesis: The E galaxy is actively assembling its mass through low-metallicity gas accretion and minor mergers within an unsettled, turbulent disc.
claims.experiment: Mapped the 2D spatially resolved gas-phase metallicity, [O III] and H-alpha kinematics, performed 2-Gaussian kinematic decomposition of E and L7, and compared warm ionised gas kinematics with ALMA [C II] cold gas maps.
claims.result: Found a ~0.7 dex (0.1 dex/kpc) metallicity gradient with lowest metallicity (12+log(O/H) ~ 7.8) in the gas-rich northwest where velocity isolines twist, high intrinsic velocity dispersion (median sigma_0 = 113 km s^-1, v/sigma_0 ~ 1), larger [O III] than [C II] velocity dispersion by up to 2-3x in the south/east, and a redshifted (+250 km s^-1) foreground companion L7.
claims.finding: The metallicity gradient and kinematic distortions in E are best explained by pristine gas accretion and an ongoing pre-collision minor merger with L7 in an unsettled, turbulent disc.

evidence.quote: showing inhomogeneities in the ISM properties at subkiloparsec scales, and a metallicity gradient (∼ 0.1 dex/kpc) that can be explained by accretion of low metallicity gas from the intergalactic medium. The kinematic maps also depict an unsettled disc characterised by deviations from regular rotation, elevated turbulence, and indications of a possible precollision minor merger.

evidence.loc: 6.2.1. Metallicity gradient and evidence of gas accretion in the E galaxy
evidence.quote: Therefore, while we cannot rule out completely the merging scenario, the ionised gas, metallicity, and kinematic maps presented here favour the gas accretion scenario in the E galaxy.

why_this_data.value: JWST/NIRSpec IFU covers rest-frame UV and main optical emission lines (including H-alpha at z = 6.9, the highest redshift accessible to NIRSpec) with ~0.5 kpc spatial resolution over a ~17 x 17 kpc^2 field around SPT0311-58.

evidence.quote: The JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations presented here cover the rest-frame UV wavelengths and main optical emission lines of SPT0311–58 (i.e. ∼ 0.13 – 0.67 µm). This allows us to characterise the physical and kinematic properties of the warm ionised gas component of its ISM at subkpc scales (i.e. ∼ 0.5 kpc) over a field of view of ∼ 17 × 17 kpc 2 .

why_this_method.value: Used the Curti et al. (2017, 2020b) metallicity calibration because it covers the observed metallicity range well with low scatter; used bootstrap for cluster velocity dispersion because it is more robust for small samples.

evidence.quote: This calibration is based on local samples, but it has the advantage of covering well the metallicity range observed in the system, and it shows relatively low scatter.
The bootstrap estimate is preferred over the standard deviation (507 km s −1 ), as it is more robust for small samples (Beers et al. 1990).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Outflow origin for component L7 or for the E galaxy metallicity gradient: rejected because BIC did not support a third outflow component, L7 is redshifted while lying in front of dusty E, and no spectral outflow signatures or minor-axis gradients are seen.

evidence.loc: 3.3.3. Identification of L7 at z ∼ 6.9 via 2D kinematic decomposition
evidence.quote: The fact the L7 is redshifted with respect to E excludes the possibility that the detected emission is due to an outflow.

evidence.loc: 6.2.1. Metallicity gradient and evidence of gas accretion in the E galaxy
evidence.quote: However, we do not see any clear evidence for outflows in our spectra. Moreover, if an outflow were present (or had been active in recent times), its most likely orientation would be along the minor axis, which is perpendicular to the direction of the metallicity gradient.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Major merger of ES and EN as the cause of the E galaxy metallicity gradient: disfavoured compared to gas accretion because [O III] and [C II] velocity fields are smooth on large scales without double velocity dispersion peaks or separate nuclear rotation.

evidence.loc: 6.2.1. Metallicity gradient and evidence of gas accretion in the E galaxy
evidence.quote: However, the kinematic properties in the main structure of E do not show evidence for two kinematically distinct objects, such as peaks in the velocity dispersion map, or rotation associated with their nuclear regions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Post-starburst interpretation for the discrepancy between SFR(FIR) and SFR(H-alpha) in the W galaxy: rejected in favour of heavy dust obscuration because W is extremely dusty with high nebular attenuation.

evidence.quote: we are dealing with an extremely dusty galaxy, we favour the star-forming interpretation, and explain the discrepancy between the SFR(Hα) and SFR(FIR) as due to heavy dust attenuation.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Disc fragmentation origin for L7: rejected because L7 is kinematically decoupled (+250 km s^-1) from E.

evidence.loc: 6.2.2. Kinematic evidence for an unsettled disc structure at redshift ∼ 7
evidence.quote: First, this significant kinematic decoupling rules out that L7 has been formed by disc fragmentation in contrast to the clumps identified by Spilker et al. (2022) at submm wavelengths.

limitations_admitted.value: Stellar masses for the newly discovered z ~ 6.9 galaxies lack MIRI photometry and may be systematically overestimated by ~0.4 dex; systematic model uncertainties on stellar masses are factors of 1.5-2.

evidence.quote: The quoted stellar mass errors correspond to the uncertainties in the fit due to flux errors, but they do not include systematic uncertainties associated with the model assumptions, which are estimated to be about factors of 1.5-2.

We also note that recent work has shown that stellar masses inferred by SED fitting without MIRI photometry may be overestimated by ∼ 0.4 dex for sources at the high-redshift of SPT0311–58 (Papovich et al. 2023; Wang et al. 2024).

limitations_admitted.value: Absolute fluxes from NIRSpec apertures are subject to uncertainties from irregular source morphologies, detector artefacts, edge effects (for C3, L3, L5), and unconsolidated instrument calibration.

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA tclean imaging parameters (weighting/robustness, clean threshold, uv-coverage) are not specified in the paper, relying on previously published reductions in Marrone et al. (2018) and Spilker et al. (2022).
The K-S test for virialisation is highly sensitive to the adopted systemic velocity of galaxy W, which differs by up to 700 km s^-1 between [C II], optical lines, and Pa-alpha.
